answer: Each identity registers one tundra relay and locks a 90-credit bond. Each epoch it files a falcon signal log: tag serial, strength, and timestamp. An auditor recomputes the expected signal from the tundra table; a missing, copied, or reused log burns bond and fee. First filing costs 30; the kth by one funder costs 30+8(k-1), so the 1,000th costs 8,022. Thus 1,000 fakes cost 4,026,000 plus 90,000 bonds. A rented-falcon ring fails because one tag fits only one sector at one timestamp, and a duplicate burns both bonds. An honest operator files once for 30 and recovers its bond if clean.
